title: Vessel Traffic Services (VTS)
description: Test your understanding of Vessel Traffic Services, vessel reporting, VTS communications, traffic organization, navigational assistance and practical operations in busy waterways.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a Vessel Traffic Service?
options: To improve the safety and efficiency of vessel traffic and help protect the environment
To replace the bridge team during port approaches
To provide technical maintenance instructions to vessels
To approve charter parties for ships entering the area
questions.explanation: A VTS is established to improve vessel-traffic safety and efficiency and to support protection of the marine environment.

questions.question: Who normally establishes or authorizes a Vessel Traffic Service?
options: An individual shipowner
A competent authority
The vessel's classification society
The local ship agent
questions.explanation: A VTS is implemented under the responsibility of a competent authority.

questions.question: Which communication method is commonly used between vessels and a VTS centre?
options: VHF radio
NAVTEX transmission
Emergency position-indicating radio beacon
Engine-room telephone
questions.explanation: VHF radio is commonly used for vessel reports, traffic information and operational communication with VTS.

questions.question: Which party remains responsible for the safe navigation of a vessel inside a VTS area?
options: The VTS operator
The port agent
The master and bridge team
The harbour authority's finance department
questions.explanation: Participation in VTS does not transfer responsibility for safe navigation away from the master and bridge team.

questions.question: What is a VTS area?
options: A defined geographical area in which a Vessel Traffic Service is provided
Any sea area covered by the vessel's radar
The restricted area around the ship's bridge
A designated anchorage used only by tankers
questions.explanation: A VTS area is a defined and formally established geographical area in which VTS services are delivered.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a VTS Information Service?
options: To ensure that essential information is available for onboard navigational decision-making
To take direct control of a vessel's steering system
To arrange pilotage contracts for each arriving vessel
To calculate the vessel's cargo stability
questions.explanation: An Information Service provides timely information that supports navigational decisions onboard.

questions.question: When is a Navigational Assistance Service most likely to be useful?
options: When a vessel requires support with onboard navigational decision-making
When a vessel requires spare parts for its main engine
When a charterer requests a new cargo nomination
When the crew needs assistance completing customs declarations
questions.explanation: Navigational Assistance Service supports onboard navigational decision-making and may monitor the effect of those decisions.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a Traffic Organization Service?
options: To prevent dangerous traffic situations and support safe and efficient traffic movement
To inspect the vessel's lifesaving appliances
To assign crew members to bridge watches
To determine which company owns each vessel
questions.explanation: Traffic Organization Service manages traffic movements to reduce congestion and prevent dangerous situations.

questions.question: Why are vessels required to report at designated reporting points in some VTS areas?
options: To provide updated information about identity, position, movement and intentions
To request permission to use the vessel's radar
To confirm that the cargo has been insured
To transmit the vessel's engine-maintenance records
questions.explanation: Reports help the VTS maintain an accurate traffic picture and provide relevant information and organization.

questions.question: Which combination of equipment may contribute to the traffic picture at a VTS centre?
options: Radar, AIS, VHF and CCTV
Echo sounder, oily-water separator and NAVTEX
Gyrocompass, incinerator and sewage-treatment plant
Ballast pumps, GPS and emergency generator
questions.explanation: VTS centres commonly integrate information from radar, AIS, radio communications, cameras and other surveillance systems.

questions.question: A vessel enters a mandatory VTS area without making the required initial report. What is the primary operational concern?
options: The VTS may not have accurate information about the vessel's position, movement and intentions
The vessel's AIS will automatically stop transmitting
The vessel's classification certificate becomes invalid
The pilot station must permanently refuse service
questions.explanation: Without the required report, the VTS traffic picture may be incomplete, reducing its ability to provide timely information and organize traffic.

questions.question: Two vessels are approaching a narrow channel from opposite directions. The VTS assigns different entry times to avoid meeting in the narrowest section. Which service is being provided?
options: Navigational Assistance Service
Information Service
Traffic Organization Service
Search and Rescue Service
questions.explanation: Coordinating entry times and traffic sequence is an example of Traffic Organization Service.

questions.question: A vessel experiences a gyrocompass failure while approaching a congested port and requests assistance from VTS. Which response best describes the role of VTS?
options: VTS may provide relevant navigational information and assistance, while the master retains responsibility for navigation
VTS automatically becomes responsible for conning the vessel
VTS may remotely operate the vessel's rudder
VTS must order the crew to abandon the bridge
questions.explanation: VTS may assist the vessel's decision-making, but responsibility for the vessel's safe navigation remains onboard.

questions.question: A VTS operator observes that two vessels are developing a close-quarters situation, but neither has reported any concern. What is the most appropriate initial action?
options: Provide timely traffic information and establish communication as appropriate
Wait until the vessels collide before making contact
Transmit an SSAS alert on behalf of both vessels
Immediately cancel both vessels' statutory certificates
questions.explanation: The operator should provide relevant, timely information and interact with the traffic according to local procedures.

questions.question: A vessel receives traffic information from VTS that conflicts with observations made by radar and visual bearings. What should the bridge team do?
options: Cross-check all available information and clarify the discrepancy with VTS
Ignore the vessel's own radar because VTS information is always correct
Alter course immediately without assessing the situation
Switch off AIS to prevent further conflicting information
questions.explanation: VTS information is an aid and should be checked against onboard observations and all other available means.

questions.question: A tanker reports a steering failure inside a busy VTS area. Which information is most urgent for the VTS operator to establish?
options: The vessel's position, movement, limitations and immediate intentions
The vessel's next dry-docking date
The price paid for the vessel's bunker fuel
The number of crew members due to sign off
questions.explanation: Position, movement, manoeuvring limitations and intentions are essential for assessing the developing traffic risk.

questions.question: A vessel is instructed to maintain listening watch on a designated VTS channel but changes to another working channel without informing VTS. What is the main risk?
options: The vessel may miss urgent traffic information or operational instructions
The vessel's radar range will be reduced
Its AIS identity will automatically change
The ship will lose its International Ship Security Certificate
questions.explanation: Maintaining the required listening watch is essential so the vessel can receive urgent safety and traffic communications.

questions.question: A vessel receives a VTS message stating: 'Traffic information: outbound tanker passing the entrance in ten minutes.' How should this message normally be interpreted?
options: As information to support the bridge team's own assessment and navigational decisions
As an instruction to stop the vessel immediately
As confirmation that the tanker is required to give way
As permission to disregard the COLREGs
questions.explanation: Traffic information contributes to situational awareness but does not replace onboard assessment or COLREG obligations.

questions.question: Visibility deteriorates rapidly in a congested VTS area. Which change is most likely in VTS operations?
options: More frequent traffic monitoring, reporting and information may be required
All radar and AIS equipment should be switched off
VTS responsibility for navigation automatically replaces the master's responsibility
Vessel reports are suspended because positions cannot be observed visually
questions.explanation: Restricted visibility may require intensified monitoring, reporting and traffic-management measures.

questions.question: A master believes that a VTS traffic instruction would place the vessel in immediate danger because of an unreported machinery limitation. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Inform VTS immediately of the limitation and explain why the instruction cannot safely be followed
Follow the instruction without question because VTS assumes navigational responsibility
Ignore VTS and stop all radio communication
Comply first and report the limitation after leaving the area
questions.explanation: The master should communicate the vessel's limitations immediately. A VTS instruction does not remove the master's duty to protect the vessel.
